items.title: Suke Quto [Honey]
items.desc:
Dans les hauts plateaux de Guji, à 2 200 mètres d’altitude, Tesfaye Bekele cultive un café qui porte en lui l’âme de l’Éthiopie. Fondateur de la ferme Suke Quto, il est l’une des figures emblématique de la filière éthiopienne; agronome, visionnaire et profondément engagé dans la régénération de son territoire.
La variété Kurume est ici travaillée en Honey : la cerise dépulpée sèche lentement avec son mucilage, conférant au café une douceur enveloppante et une complexité aromatique rare.
En tasse, une sucrosité de cassonade s’ouvre sur une acidité lumineuse aux accents d’ananas, avant une final

items.title: Gato Grande [Geisha Natural CRF #7]
items.desc:
Ce Geisha Naturel de Gato Grande est produit par Yessie Hartmann et Jean-Paul Langenstein, au coeur des Tierras Altas de Chiriquí, au Panama. Installée entre 1910 et 2000 mètres d’altitude, la ferme s’inscrit dans la continuité d’une longue histoire familiale : les Hartmann cultivent le café au Panama depuis plusieurs générations et ont largement contribué à la reconnaissance des cafés et surtout des Geishas panaméens.
Notre lot met en avant une lecture particulièrement élégante du Geisha en traitement Naturel. La dégustation s’ouvre sur une pomme fraîche et croquante, avant de laisser apparaî

items.title: Santa Elena [Geisha Pinnacle]
items.desc:
Cafelino est une entreprise familiale installée à Boquete, dans les montagnes de Chiriquí. Spécialisée dans le café de spécialité durable, elle allie tradition, innovation et respect de la nature pour offrir un café d’exception.
Au cœur de l’exploitation se trouve la Finca Santa Elena, perchée entre 1 250 et 1 530 mètres d’altitude. Grâce à son terroir volcanique unique et à des méthodes de production soignées, Santa Elena produit des cafés réputés pour leur arôme riche et leur qualité exceptionnelle.
Ce magnifique geisha est sublimé par le process exclusif Pinnacle, une méthode Hybrid d’une p

items.title: Janson [Los Alpes GN195]
items.desc:
Le Geisha naturel anaérobie 72h de Los Alpes Janson est un café qui révèle une expression plus intense et fruitée de cette variété mythique. Issu des parcelles de Volcan, dans la province de Chiriqui, ce Geisha illustre le savoir-faire de Janson dans la recherche d’une tasse à la fois expressive, précise et élégante.
Le process anaérobie de 72 heures vient ici amplifier naturellement la richesse aromatique du Geisha. En filtre, la tasse s’ouvre sur des notes d’hibiscus, florales et légèrement acidulées, qui donnent immédiatement beaucoup de fraîcheur et de vivacité. Le citron apporte ensuite u

items.title: Janson [Hacienda GW190]
items.desc:
Le Geisha Washed 190 (GW190) de la Hacienda Janson n’est pas un café qui cherche à impressionner par l’exubérance. Il séduit par sa clarté et l’expression de son terroir. Issu des parcelles de Volcan, dans la province de Chiriqui, ce Geisha illustre, comme toujours avec la café Janson, une lecture élégante de cette variété mytique.
Le process lavé agit ici comme un révélateur. il retire les artifices pour laisser parler la structure aromatique intrinsèque du Geisha. Le café en filtre évoque immédiatement un thé sencha fin, avec cette texture soyeuse et cette fraîcheur végétale caractéristique.

items.title: Hacienda la Esmeralda [Montana 3NC]
items.desc:
Un Geisha Naturel qui joue sur la finesse plutôt que sur la puissance, avec une tasse particulièrement expressive où le floral et le fruité se répondent avec beaucoup de précision.
Cultivé dans les hauteurs de Cañas Verdes, au sein de la mythique Hacienda La Esmeralda, ce Montaña 3NC est issu d’un micro-lot Geisha sélectionné pour son expression aromatique. Ici, le séchage naturel est travaillé afin de concentré les sucres du fruit tout en conservant la finesse et la transparence caractéristiques des Geishas de La Esmeralda.
En tasse, le jasmin apparaît dès les premières gorgées avec une fines

items.title: Alo [Sky Project FL]
items.desc:
Issu du Sky Project d’Alo Coffee, ce lot pousse dans le village d’Alo, à Bensa. L’idée du projet est aussi simple que radicale : aller chercher des altitudes où les nuits plus fraîches ralentissent la maturation des cerises. Une maturation plus lente permet aux fruits d’accumuler davantage de sucres et de développer une expression aromatique particulièrement dense.
En tasse, le café joue sur la carte du fruit et de la fraîcheur. La pêche apparaît d’abord : pulpeuse, mûre, juteuse. Puis arrive le raisin rouge et sa sucrosité éclatante. Enfin, se dévoile la groseille avec son acidité vive.

items.title: Finca Rosma [Geisha Washed]
items.desc:
Un Geisha lavé tout en finesse, issu de la Finca Rosma à Huehuetenango. Cette ferme familiale, fondée en 1963 par Alejandro Morales est aujourd’hui dirigée par la famille Morales.
La tasse s’ouvrira sur des notes délicates de jasmin et de citron, amenant une acidité élégante. Puis, le café gagnera en douceur, des notes d’abricot sucrés accompagnées d’une texture soyeuse évoquant le lait d’amande. Un café équilibré, floral et lumineux.

items.title: Granja Paraiso 92 [Red Bourbon Advanced Washed]
items.desc:
Un espresso colombien signé Wilton Benitez, issu de la mythique Granja Paraiso 92, dans la Valle Del Cauca. Ici, le red bourbon est travaillé avec une approche expérimentale, notamment avec la fermentation contrôlée lavée qui vient pousser l’expression aromatique tout en conservant en tasse un équilibre net et précis.
En espresso, le profil s’ouvre sur une violette très expressive, puis laisse apparaître une sensation de liqueur de cerises, dense et légèrement acidulée, avant de s’étirer sur un chocolat noir plus profond. Une tasse à la fois florale, liquoreuse et structurée, où la fermentatio

items.title: Alo [Zero Fermentation Washed]
items.desc:
Derrière ce Zero Fermentation Washed, Alo cherche à retirer une étape devenue presque incontournable dans les lavés modernes : la fermentation. Les cerises mûres sont triées, dépulpées puis lavées immédiatement, sans passage en cuves. L’objectif, simple en apparence est très exigeant en pratique, il faut éviter que la fermentation ne façonne le profil aromatique et laisser la variété et le terroir s’exprimer avec le moins d’interférences possibles.
La tasse s’ouvre sur une texture aérienne, avec une première note de thé blanc qui se dévoile dans le palais. Vient alors la cerise, fraîche et aci

items.title: Elto [Elora RF8 Natural]
items.desc:
Au coeur du projet Elto Coffee, la fermentation tient un rôle de véritable levier d’expression du terroir.
Pour notre lot RF8 Naturel, les cerises fermentent naturellement dans des sacs hermétiques immergés dans une rivière, avant un séchage lent permettant de préserver la richesse aromatique développée pendant le processus.
En tasse, le café donne une sensation de douceur. La cerise vient apporter une sucrosité fruitée et éclatante ; vite suivie par la rose séchée, la tasse prend une dimension florale, délicate et parfumée. Enfin, le bubblegum prolonge la douceur dans la gourmandise, voire ve

items.title: Santa Elena [Geisha Aura]
items.desc:
Cultivé à la Santa Elena, sur les pentes du Cerro Piedra de Lino au coeur de la vallée de Boquete, ce Geisha profite d’un terroir particulièrement favorable à l’expression aromatique de la variété. C’est entre 1200 et 1550 mètres d’altitude que la ferme cultive différentes variétés d’arabica, dont le Geisha. Santa Elena est aujourd’hui porté par la famille Ameglio, dont l’histoire agricole au Panama remonte à plusieurs générations. La ferme a été acquise en 2011 par Marco et Xenia Ameglio, qui ont depuis entrepris de moderniser progressivement la plantation et leurs méthodes de production.
Sur

items.title: Jamison Savage [Caturra Washed]
items.desc:
Le Panama ne produit simplement de superbes Geishas, parce que au milieu de cette obsession pour les tasses emplie de clarté et de pureté, il existe des cafés beaucoup plus directs, plus gourmands, tout en restant équilibrés. Ce Caturra Lavé de Jamison Savage en fait partie.
La tasse commence sur quelque chose de gourmand : le chocolat au lait, puis arrive la prune rouge, avec cette sensation vive et élégante que l’on retrouve dans les cafés kenyans. Enfin, ces notes s’élargissent vers la noisette, en laissant une sensation douce et généreuse en bouche. Un Caturra qui ne cherche pas à jouer au

items.title: Los Lajones Porton [GN #23109]
items.desc: Notre lot Geisha Naturel 23109 provient de Los Lajones, la ferme de Graciano Cruz, dans la région de Boquete au Panama. La propriété en elle-même est très très intéressante. Une grande partie de son territoire reste couverte de forêt, et les plantations de café occupent notamment les secteurs plus élévés. Graciano Cruz a une approche construite autour des procédés classiques de traitement, avec une volonté de travailler le café sans chercher à le rendre artificiellement spectaculaire. Le principe est plutôt de donner au fruit et à la variété suffisamment de temps pour exprimer ce qu’ils ont a

items.title: Hacienda la Esmeralda [Lino 6HC]
items.desc:
Cultivé à haute altitude dans la région de Boquete, au Panama, au sein de la célèbre Hacienda la Esmeralda, le café Lino 6HC bénéficie d’un procédé honey avec séchage contrôlé, où le séchage des cerises avec une partie de mucilage est maîtrisé afin de préserver la complexité aromatique tout en développant douceur et profondeur. Le nom Lino ne désigne pas une variété, mais un bien lot spécifique de la ferme, en isolant des parcelles précises, Hacienda la Esmeralda vient chercher à isoler les expressions les plus intéressantes du terroir.
Notre lot Lino 6HC de Hacienda la Esmeralda est donc une

items.title: Finca Sophia [RW4 – Colibri-Poro 40 GW] – Auction Lot
items.desc:
L’équipe de Tanat Coffee est honorée de partager avec vous deux lots obtenus lors de la vente aux enchères de la Finca Sophia. Deux cafés Geisha lavés exceptionnels, qui témoignent de notre admiration pour l’engagement, la rigueur et la passion de l’équipe Finca Sophia.
Ces deux lots lavés vous feront découvrir deux profils sensoriels authentiques, mettant en valeur la pureté de la variété, le soin apporté à son terroir ainsi que la maîtrise d’un procédé de lavage d’une extrême précision.
Une acidité d’agrumes douce et vive ouvre sur des notes de mandarine, de nectarine, de bonbon au citron et

items.title: Elto [Hamasho 96h]
items.desc:
Sur les hauts plateaux de Bensa, en Éthiopie, se trouve Elto Coffee, projet d’Eliyas Dukamo et d’Atiklit Dejene. Forts tous deux d’une solide expérience dans la production de cafés d’exception en Éthiopie, ils ont créé Elto Coffee avec l’ambition de repousser les standards de qualité en mettant la lumière les terroirs de Bensa et des méthodes de lavage plus modernes.
Sur notre lot Elto Hamasho, les 96 heures de fermentation construisent une tasse d’une intensité forte, mais toujours lisible. En début de dégustation, les fruits noirs prennent la main, une myrtille juteuse, une mûre éclatante, u

items.title: Alo [Digs Project Anaerobic Honey 48h]
items.desc:
Direction les hauts plateaux de Bensa, au coeur du village d’Alo, où le producteur Tamiru Tadesse signe des cafés parmi les plus recherché d’Éthiopie. Ce lot est issu d’une fermentation anaérobie honey avec 48h de fermentation. Les cerises sont sélectionnées minutieusement avant de fermenter en environnement anaérobie pendant deux jours, permettant un développement aromatique intense ; après cette fermentation contrôlée, le café est dépulpé puis séché lentement sur lits africains, avec une partie du mucilage préservée pour apporter d’avantage de sucrosité.
Ce café est produit dans le cadre du

items.title: Gesha Village [Oma Anaerobic Natural 26/E24]
items.desc:
Issu de mythique terroir de Gesha Village, au coeur de la région de West Omo en Éthiopie, ce lot Oma G26 E24 est cultivé sur les pentes du bloc Oma, où la variété Gesha 1931 exprime tpute sa finesse. La fermentation en anaérobie naturelle de ce lot apporte une profondeur aromatique remarquable sans masquer l’identité du terroir.
En tasse, l’ouverture est aérienne. Le coquelicot vient évoquer une douceur florale, rejoint par une myrtille juteuse et l’orange vient ensuite illuminer l’ensemble d’une fraîcheur vive, laissant une finale longue et élégante.
Chaque tasse évoluera en refroidissant, dé

items.title: Janson [Hacienda GW121]
items.desc:
Découvrez ce magnifique lot 121 Geisha lavé issue de la plantation Hacienda Janson. Il se dévoilera en tasse un café expressif et pur, caractéristique des hauts plateaux de la région de Chiriqui, au Panama, nichée sur les hauts plateaux de Volcan.
Un café d’une grande douceur et élégance, sa texture soyeuse, sa finesse florale rappelant le chèvrefeuille et sa finale longue abricot en font un grand cru d’exception.

items.title: Alo Bore [Washed]
items.desc:
Ce lot vient des hauteurs du Guji, en Éthiopie, où Tamiru Tadesse cultive la variété 74158 à plus de 2000 mètres d’altitude.
Traité en lavé, il offre une tasse nette et florale, où les fleurs blanches laissent place à la pêche, avant une finale vive de pamplemousse.

items.title: Choco Nuts
items.desc: Choco Nuts is our latest Brazilian espresso, produced by Adriano Muñiz and his family at Agropecuária Muñiz in Sul de Minas. This anaerobic natural Catucaí has everything we enjoy in a classic Brazilian coffee, with plenty of sweetness, a round body and a creamy texture. Expect notes of hazelnut, milk chocolate and vanilla, making it a great everyday espresso that also works really well with milk.

items.title: Pillow Talk
items.desc: Los Nogales does decaf a little differently. This Caturra is grown, processed and decaffeinated at the farm in Pitalito, giving Oscar Hernandez and his team control over the coffee from cherry to finished decaf. It’s bright and sweet, with starfruit, agave and rosemary. A decaf we’d happily drink whether we were looking for one or not. * Due to the decaffeination process, the beans may have an unusual colour. This is completely normal and does not affect the quality of the coffee.

items.title: Peachy Daze
items.desc: Peachy Daze is back, a clean washed Ethiopian from the Chelbesa washing station in Gedeb, where heirloom varieties grow at 2173 masl. The cup is light and delicate, with white peach and lemon up front, black tea through the middle and a soft elderflower finish.

items.title: Blackberry Dust
items.desc: Blackberry Dust is a late-harvest natural Ethiopian coffee from the Buku Abel washing station in Guji, which arrived in Europe just a few weeks ago. Around 400 smallholder farmers contribute to the station, growing heirloom varieties at elevations between 1,900 and 2,100 masl. The cup is fruity and sweet, with notes of blackberry, wild strawberry and blueberry yoghurt, followed by a soft, creamy finish.

items.title: Macaron
items.desc: One of our all-time favourites from Johan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, this natural Red Bourbon has become one of those coffees we’re always excited to bring back. It goes through an advanced anaerobic natural process and comes out big, juicy and seriously sweet, with strawberry jam, raspberry macaron and buttercream.

items.title: Sticky Pudding
items.desc: Our Christmas coffee is here! This year we’ve worked with CATA Export in Colombia to create something inspired by the festive season. This bourbon undergoes a co-fermentation with cinnamon, cardamom, mandarin and cherry, giving it a distinctive profile while keeping plenty of sweetness in the cup. Expect notes of cinnamon, cardamom and fresh fir – a very festive profile.

items.title: Cream Donut
items.desc: Cream Donut is a collaboration with Cata Export and producer Franky Hoyos in Colombia. A yeast-inoculated natural Caturra Chiroso developed for DAK through rounds of back-and-forth trialling. It’s an unusual coffee that has somehow become one of our staples and a bestseller, loved for its distinct character and the ridiculously good flat white it makes. Expect chocolate milk, cherry-filled doughnut and vanilla, whether you brew it as filter or espresso.

items.title: Plum Butter
items.desc: Plum Butter is a natural from Bulambuli in East Uganda, produced with our long-time partners at Ibero. It’s a profile we don’t come across often from Uganda: deep, smooth and fruit-forward, with dark plum, grape cordial and cacao. Rich without becoming too heavy.

items.title: Berry Blues
items.desc: Berry Blues is back. We’ve had this coffee in different variations over the years, sometimes under Berry Blues, sometimes as Blueberry Boom, and it remains a favourite across the DAK team for its big fruit character and how much fun it is to drink. This year’s harvest from Esayas Beriso is an anaerobic natural, grown high in Oromia, Ethiopia, and slowly dried in the shade. There’s plenty of dark fruit and a boozy edge: grape soda up front, myrtle liquor behind it, and a cashew-butter richness that gives the cup its buttery body and creamy mouthfeel.

items.title: Darling
items.desc: Darling comes from Danche Washing Station in Gedeb, and it’s one of the more delicate Ethiopians we’ve had this year. The coffee goes through a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation before being washed, resulting in a cup with good clarity despite the additional fermentation. Wild florals lead, followed by peach iced tea and a black-tea finish. Light, elegant and very tea-like.

items.title: Rhubarb Fizz
items.desc: Our next Kenyan of the season, and one of our favourites this year. Rhubarb Fizz is a washed AA from Ndimi Factory in Kirinyaga, bringing together SL28, SL34, Batian and Ruiru 11 from the surrounding smallholder farms. Juicy and layered, with rhubarb soda, blackcurrant and orange.

items.title: Hazel Nuts
items.desc: Hazel Nuts is a natural Catuaí from Chinacla in the Marcala region of Honduras, grown by our longtime partners Marysabel Caballero and Moises Herrera. We’ve been buying their coffees for years, and this is one we particularly like for espresso. Round and silky, with hazelnut, cacao nibs and blackberry, plus a touch of booziness that we really enjoy. Especially good with milk.

items.title: Silky Way
items.desc: Silky Way is another coffee from Jhoan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, the same family behind Macaron. This time it’s their washed Pink Bourbon, with a completely different side of the farm showing up in the cup. Lemongrass, white florals and crisp green apple, with a bright, sparkling quality that suits the name pretty well.

items.title: Poppy Soda
items.desc: Poppy Soda is a Pink Bourbon from Sebastián Ramírez at El Placer in Quindío, Colombia. It goes through a pretty elaborate washed process, but the cup itself is all about clarity. Lemonade, jasmine tea and ripe peach, with a bright, almost soda-like quality that makes the name make sense.

items.title: The Alchemist
items.desc: The Alchemist is one of the staples in our line-up and a coffee we source directly from Gasharu Farms in Nyamasheke, Rwanda. An anaerobic natural Red Bourbon that changes quite a bit depending on how you brew it. Espresso pushes the cacao forward; filter opens up the tropical fruit and jammy sweetness. Complex, rich and particularly good with milk.

items.title: Jazz fruits
items.desc: Jazz Fruits is a staple in our lineup and one we try to keep around all year, whenever the harvest allows. We source this community lot from Daye Bensa each year for its fruity, easy-going profile and how well it works as espresso, especially with milk. Strawberry, white chocolate and mandarin in the cup. Named after the Jazz Fruits playlists on Spotify.

items.title: Mucho Berry Blend
items.desc:
Mucho Berry
Momos Coffee’s fourth signature blend
Ethiopia is widely known as one of the coffee-growing regions loved by many people. In particular, Ethiopian coffees processed by the natural method are recognized for their diverse berry-like aromas and their broad appeal, making them enjoyable for a wide range of drinkers.
Inspired by these berry characteristics, the fourth signature blend, Mucho Berry, was created to express rich and attractive berry-forward aromas.

items.title: Fruity Bonbon Blend
items.desc:
Fruity Bonbon
Momos Coffee’s second signature blend
In 2009, when specialty coffee was first encountered in the United States, coffees with bright acidity and fruit-like aromas were still unfamiliar to many people. However, drawn to the diverse aromas and new flavors found in high-quality coffee, Momos Coffee introduced its second signature blend, Fruity Bonbon, to share the distinct character and appeal of specialty coffee.

items.title: Es Chocolat Blend
items.desc:
Es Chocolat
Momos Coffee’s first signature blend
Es Chocolat, the very first signature blend introduced by Momos Coffee, was developed at a time when dark-roasted coffees reminiscent of chocolate were the mainstream style. It reflects the early days of Momos Coffee and the intention to create a coffee that could be enjoyed and loved by everyone.

JUICY - BLACKBERRY - ROSE

items.desc:
This ultra limited coffee came direct from Diego Bermudez as part of his Hachi project, and this is certainly one of the more uniquely processed coffees we've ever offered, all while maintaining clean, lush fruit flavors. This coffee is ripe and big with cranberry and tart cherry flavors, along with crushed pineapple and glimmering caramel notes.

items.title: Diamond Reserve
items.desc:
Fresh Colombian geshas are bursting onto the scene, and this latest addition is a knockout. Diamond Reserve gesha brings cherry & apricot flavor combined with the tropical charm of guava. We also tasted peach, berries, and the depth of caramel. This went to our monthly subscribers last month, and we have a handful of bags rested & ready to drink from that date!

items.title: Las Perlitas Chiroso
items.desc:
Welcome back Perlitas! This is our second edition of Perlitas Chiroso and we are excited to share it with you. Usually Perlitas is a combo of caturra, pink bourbon, etc, but Stephen from The Coffee Quest sent us this pure chiroso version and we loved it. The Chiroso variety is expanding rapidly in Colombia, and we're excited to bring in even more as new trees mature. Renowned for its flavor quality, this relative of Ethiopian landrace varieties is a beautiful, clean coffee with flavors of orange, currant, and a warm spice reminiscent of clove. Also available green!

items.title: Alpenglow
items.desc:
As we say goodbye to our Zuria Blend, we present the all new Alpenglow, Prodigal's limited fall blend. The washed Ethiopian brings ripe fruits, the chiroso brings the balance and warmth, and the glamorous gesha adds notable depth and complexity. The flavors are dazzling pineapple, pulpy, ripe orange, and tart cranberry. This coffee has no business being this good, and we loved formulating it for you!

items.title: Gesha Harmony
items.desc:
We are absolutely thrilled with this just-landed Colombian gesha, hailing from a farm connected to past menu star Fabiola Ortega (Higueron, Tabor, Velvet Bliss). Fabiola's daughter Marilin Muñoz produced this coffee, and its ripe peach, grape, and cola flavors are a knockout. We also tasted cranberry, jasmine, and syrupy apricot. Scott brewed a stash of this coffee in Panama at the World of Coffee event, and the reception was wonderful. Our October subscribers received this coffee first, but we couldn't hold it back for long, so now it's available for everyone!

items.title: El Itacayo DRD Geisha
items.desc:
With great joy and sadness we are announcing this final Honduran coffee of 2026, and it is tremendous. Angel Arturo Paz set aside a tiny bit of his special Dark Room Dried (DRD) geisha for us, and we are supremely honored. This coffee is ripe and saturated, with exotic yet refined flavors. We've never put "watermelon" as a tasting note on a Prodigal release before, but this coffee has earned its pedigree. With huge pineapple, red wine, and watermelon, this is truly a special coffee. We also tasted grape jelly, strawberry, rhubarb, and a lovely, tart acidity.

items.title: Chelbesa Danche
items.desc:
Chelbesa Danche is practically a household name in specialty coffee, and this lot is about as clean & fruity as it gets. The flavors are layered orange and tart cherry, with even a hint of pineapple, grape, and raspberry. The aromas are rose and powdered sugary blueberries. This is classic, washed Ethiopian coffee.
This coffee is named for the Danche washing station where it's produced. Approximately 800 farmers deliver their coffee cherries to this washing station, each farming 2-3 hectares of land at 2200 meters.

items.title: Habtamu Danche
items.desc:
Roasted just a touch darker than our filter version , this espresso roast makes fantastic straight shots and Americanos.
This is the year of Habtamu! We roasted this gorgeous washed Ethiopian for our monthly subscribers in July, and now it's available for everyone. Ethiopia is having a banner year, and Habtamu is knocking it out of the park. We're loving this coffee's big, ripe apricot coupled with a touch of pineapple and jasmine-like florals.

items.title: Mulu
items.desc:
Mulu Espresso is Prodigal's new seasonal blend, composed of 100% fresh Ethiopian washed & natural coffees, roasted just a touch darker for espresso. This is a super fun coffee, combining everything we love about classic Ethiopian flavors. Look for citrus and florals from the washed component and rich cherry flavor from the natural. Mulu is punchy and ripe and makes great straight espresso and americanos.

items.title: DEAR COFFEE BUYER
items.desc:
Dear Coffee Buyer by Ryan Brown is the first ever book dedicated to the profession of green coffee buying. Brown's vivid descriptions and engaging prose make readers feel like they’re right there with him: tagging along to taste hundreds of coffee samples during a twenty-hour stop in Guatemala, feeling his nervous excitement when he takes a spontaneous buying trip to Honduras with little more than a backpack, and sharing his frustration and determination to find farmers and exporters willing to offer exceptional coffees.

items.title: Milk Blend
items.desc:
This is our signature Milk Blend, composed primarily of a clean, soft Colombian caturra, blended with something a little more sparkly to keep things interesting. The second component changes regularly as we rotate quickly through fresh green coffee, but this blend remains consistent and always optimized for milk drinks.
Make sure to check that the roast date you've selected is what you're looking for — The UPCOMING ROAST date is listed under the tasting notes at the top of this product page, or shop from our rested selection if available!

items.title: Boulder Blend
items.desc:
We love blending coffees. By selectively combining washed and natural/honey-processed coffees, Boulder Blend unites ripe and fruity flavors with clean, juicy qualities.
We don’t buy coffees specifically for blending. Instead, we craft every batch of Boulder Blend from our limited headline coffees.
Boulder Blend’s components may change slightly week to week, but it's always fruity, bright and balanced — a coffee you'll reach for every day.

items.title: Second Slice / Costa Rica
items.desc: Second Slice is pure comfort in a cup. Warm cinnamon and baked apple pie bring the sweetness, while toasted pecan adds a rich, nutty finish. A cozy Costa Rican coffee that tastes like going back for another piece.

items.title: Cherry Wild / Colombia
items.desc:
Cherry Wild is a celebration of Colombia’s vibrant coffee spirit—lively, sweet, and just a little
untamed. Bursting with ripe cherry brightness, the cup carries the rich, spiced depth of fruitcake, lifted by a sparkling hint of tangerine.

jasmine / grapefruit / mandarin orange / white tea

items.title: Hideaway / Dark
items.desc: Hideaway is your go-to dark roast for those moments when only the richest, most comforting coffee will do.

items.title: Daydream / Light
items.desc:
Let your thoughts drift with Daydream.
Daydream is your invitation to pause and reflect, perfect for moments when you need a gentle lift.

items.title: Two Wheel / House
items.desc:
Kick start your day with a dynamic ride.
Two Wheel is like a morning ride through your favourite part of town, energizing and full of life.

items.title: Off Hours / Decaf Coffee
items.desc:
Unwind anytime with a decaf that’s rich in flavour, without the caffeine.
Off Hours is perfect for those late-night moments or anytime you need a break without the buzz; it’s decaf done right.

items.title: Homebody / Medium
items.desc: Homebody is like your favourite spot on the couch – always welcoming and perfectly cozy, ideal for thriving in your safe space.

items.title: KENYA Gondo AA
items.desc:
Gondo AA comes from Gondo Factory in Murang’a County, on the western slopes of the Aberdare Mountains. The factory is one of three managed by the New Kiriti Farmers Cooperative Society, and it receives cherry from 727 smallholder farmers in the surrounding area. Most farms are small, often averaging around 250 coffee trees, and the cool temperatures, regular rainfall, and deep red volcanic soils help the coffee mature slowly.

items.title: COLOMBIA La Violeta Sidra
items.desc:
La Violeta is one of Rafael Aya Martínez’s farms in La Florida, near Timaná in southern Huila. This year, we stayed overnight on the farm, walked the land with Rafael, cupped through his coffees together, and visited his new café in Timaná. The visit gave us a clearer view of how his work connects cultivation, processing, and the local coffee culture he is helping build around his own coffees.

items.desc:

items.desc:
From the highlands of Shale, a small village near Worka in Southern Ethiopia, this washed lot comes from Tadese Teko’s eight-hectare farm—a size notably larger than the regional average. His farm sits between 1,780 and 2,100 masl, rooted in deep red clay soils and surrounded by dense native vegetation.

items.desc:
Chiroso Imperial is the result of a partnership between four neighboring coffee growing families of Hub Management Palestina, including Ramón Gómez of Finca La Moreira. Grown on loamy clay to clay soils with volcanic ash and gravelly sectors, the coffee benefits from shade practices that protect the soil and support consistent development.

items.desc:
Finca El Mesón sits in the vereda of Berlin in southern Huila, where steep ridgelines and shifting soils mark the transition between Colombia’s mountain systems. Reaching the farm means a long drive along winding roads before the landscape opens to exposed slopes and narrow ridges planted with Pink Bourbon.

items.desc:
After returning to her family’s farm, El Silencio in Filandia, Sara Gutiérrez embraced innovation, challenging tradition with experimental fermentation. Now a Cup of Excellence judge and local coffee leader, she’s shaping Colombia’s coffee future.
This honey-processed Caturra is co-fermented with beer hops, adding depth and aromatic complexity. After 24-hour cherry rest and 48-hour tank fermentation, slow drying on raised beds preserves its structure. The hops subtly enhance the coffee’s profile, introducing a unique layer of flavor.

items.title: COLOMBIA Finca Pensilvania Laurina
items.desc:
Laurina, also known as Bourbon Pointu, is a rare natural mutation within Arabica, distinguished by its naturally low caffeine content and unique plant structure. The variety produces smaller seeds and lower yields, making it uncommon in commercial production and more demanding to cultivate.
At 1760 meters in La Llanada, Huila, Eduar Sain Muñoz grows Laurina under conditions that support steady cherry development and careful field management. items.title: KENYA Gondo AB
items.desc:
Gondo is one of three factories managed by the New Kiriti FCS in Murang’a County, on the western slopes of the Aberdare Mountains. The region’s cool temperatures, high elevation, and deep red volcanic soils support the dense seed structure and vivid acidity that have made Murang’a one of Kenya’s most respected coffee producing areas.

items.desc:
The Pacamara Natural from Finca Majahual is one of the farm’s most distinctive offerings. Grown at high elevation in the Los Naranjos Valley, these large-bean Pacamara cherries are selectively harvested at peak ripeness and naturally processed entirely on-site. By keeping processing at elevation, without transporting cherries to distant mills, the farm preserves the integrity of the fruit, resulting in cleaner, juicier, and brighter cups.

items.desc:
The Red Bourbon Washed from Finca Majahual represents the farm’s classic expression of El Salvador’s most iconic varietal. Grown between 1,500 and 1,800 meters in the cool microclimate of the Los Naranjos Valley, this coffee is carefully handpicked, fully washed, and dried with meticulous attention to detail to highlight its crisp structure and balanced sweetness. In the cup: red apple, caramel, and plum.

items.desc:
Karinga is one of several washing stations operated by Gitwe Farmers Cooperative Society Ltd in Kenya's Central Highlands. Established in 1983, it receives cherry from around 500 active smallholder members in Kimaruri, Kariungu, Gachuha, and Mugalwa villages. The factory sits at 1840 masl in Kiambu County, where cool temperatures slow cherry maturation and help build the dense structure found in the best washed Kenyan coffees.

Our relationship with Patrick Murray is long enough that we have tasted this project through strong harvests and difficult ones. That context matters to us. Majahual is not a flat farm. It rises and falls through slopes, ridges and shallow depressions that are not quite valleys. El Ciprés sits in one of those folds. It comes from cherries delivered by local farmers in the surrounding area and is processed at 2150 masl. The cup is round, balanced, and complex, with baked apple, peach jam, orange, biscuit, jasmine, plum, rosehip, red currant, and black tea in the profile.

El Vergel Estate sits in Fresno, Tolima, where Elías and Shady Bayter have spent more than a decade refining their approach to coffee. What began as a family farm has grown into Forest Coffee, a network connecting more than 250 coffee-growing families through a focus on quality, innovation and transparent trade.
This lot is naturally decaffeinated using the sugarcane process in Colombia. Green coffee is gently steamed before caffeine is removed with naturally derived ethyl acetate from sugarcane. The beans are then steamed again to remove any remaining residue, preserving the coffee's sweetnes

items.title: Hanan Million Natural | Guji, Ethiopia
items.desc:
Local landrace varieties carrying the particular character of Buku Hambella. Hanan founded ASHKIM with her mother, Asha Yuya, the name honouring Asha and her sister Kimiya.
The fermentation that happens inside a drying coffee fruit is microbially complex and environmentally responsive, and the difference between a natural that sings and one that doesn't comes down to decisions made on the drying bed across weeks. Hanan's lands in the expressive register: purple haribo gummies, bubblegum, white tea are things we’ve been picking up with this one.

items.title: Moata Raya Lunar Honey | Agaro, Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot is a fun experiment using 74110 local landrace (and catalogued by JARC) grown by smallholder farmers on garden plots in Agaro. Moata bought this fruit from locals as he doesn't have a farm, but he still wanted to work through this processing idea - and we get to enjoy the results together. This lot is a honey, where Moata used a hand disk pulper with no further soak, and laid the parchment out on raised beds, covered with shade mesh during the day, and opening the netting at dusk and overnight, resulting in things like nougaty white mulberry, taffy and oolong.

items.title: Basha Bekele Natural (minis) | Sidama, Ethiopia
items.desc: Variety 74158 grown by 1st place COE winner (2024), Basha Bekele, on his farm in Bombe, Bensa, Sidama. Proccessed as a natural with whole fruit dried on raised beds. This lot is particularily special as it features the smallest screen sizes, not normally exportable. Moata, who works with Crop to Cup took it upon himself to painstakingly re-sort these 'minis', with the idea that these smaller fruits have outsized flavour. We're inclined to agree.

Kai and Jannette Janson are the main people behind Janson Family Estates - and are two of the loveliest people in Panama. They've been running the operations at the farm, located in the town of Volcan, for many years now - preceded by generations in the Janson family.

items.title: Danche Hydro Honey
items.desc: We're welcoming in a new lot that we haven't worked with this producer before, and we've got to say - it's something very special! This is from the Danche Washing Station, in Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, very closely located to the Chelbesa stations. The cherry here is sourced from 810 registered growers in the villages Danche and Kubi, in Gedeo zone, Gedeb. The average elevation of the farms lies at around 2100 Meters Above Sea level on rich and fertile red soil in a semi-forested environment, and harvest takes place between November and January. items.title: Kiandu AA Washed
items.desc:
Great, classic washed Kenyan coffees are getting harder and harder to find unfortunately. Subtle changes to farming practices, environmental reasons, and changes to varieties mean that the classic Kenyan profile of old is much more rare. This Kiandu AA lot is a great representation of how great and fruity Kenyan Washed coffees can be!

items.desc:
Ever since first trying Ivan and Priscilla's coffee's in 2022, we loved what they produced. Their elusive Washed Geisha is a rare lot that speaks for itself in quality and elegance - something super special, and worth appreciating!
Grown in Bambito, nearby Volcan in Panama (just off the road leading to Cerro Punta), the land where their geisha grows goes up the mountain to around 1800m above sea level. items.title: Alo Main Station Dark Room Dry Natural
items.desc:
From the main station of Alo Village, and a producer we've worked with for several years now, comes a very special lot that represents how much Tamiru Tadesse has pushed processing at Alo. This lot is a classic natural, without extra fermentation but has a special dark room drying. Tamiru built these dark rooms for drying coffee a few years ago, but has expanded them recently to accomodate more lots, and we were lucky enough to get this one, lot #34. This whole 17kg lot has been sent to us, and we're happy to share it with you now.

items.title: Mama Sierra Caturra Washed
items.desc:
This is your answer to a daily coffee that's good on price, giving a dependable flavour profile, and enjoyable every day without being too much. Mama Sierra, led by Sirley Pulgarin of The Coffee Quest Colombia, is a remarkable project empowering women coffee farmers in the community of Giraldo, Antioquia. With 15 motivated members, the project began in March 2021, initiated by Yessica Parra and later taken forward by Sirley. The goal has always been to break barriers limiting women’s access to resources and training in coffee production.

items.title: Kotowa Las Brujas Geisha Clean Natural
items.desc:
This year is the first year we're buying from Kotowa Farms in Boquete, and we're absolutely thrilled to offer this amazing Geisha from their Las Brujas farm lot 26-094!
This lot in particular is their outstanding Geisha, which was processed with a "Natural" process, although the result in the cup is something that reminds us much more of a washed. We had confirmed with the farm that it was infact a natural, even though it does appear more washed. This coffee was picked on the 3rd of February, and left in bags overnight before being laid straight onto raised african beds, spread into a thin 5cm

items.title: Chilaka Anaerobic Natural
items.desc:
Tamiru Tadesse is a coffee supplier who has been in the coffee business for the last eight years. He works with about 200 farmers in Delo Kebele, Bensa zone of the Sidama region. He collects about 182,000 kilograms of red cherry from an estimated 80 hectares of land owned by the farmers. Tamiru processes anaerobic and natural coffee which is dried on a raised bed with mesh wire. He then sells his coffee on the international market, mostly in China. However, he says, he was interested to have new market destinations and promote the unique flavours of Bensa coffee.

items.title: Altieri Pre-dry Natural Geisha DFM
items.desc:
This is our first year visiting and buying from the Altieri farm in Boquete, and it was an absolute treat. Getting to see their facilities, and cup their outstanding lots from a variety of processes and elevations is really impressive! We purchased a few lots from them, and the first to be released is this pre-dry natural Geisha.
This lot is from their Tom lot - it sits around 1700m above sea level at Alto Quiel, in Boquete, Panama. It covers an area of approximately 1 hectare of volcanic soil where Geisha Green Tip grows. It is adjacent to the protected area of the Volcan Baru national park,

items.title: Guji Rassa Washed
items.desc:
This is a classic washed Ethiopian coffee that ticks all the boxes. You can imagine that when someone says "washed Ethiopian coffee" you have a profile in mind - this is exactly that - nothing more, nothing less.
Grown from 2000-2200masl in the village of Rassa, in the Guji region of Ethiopia, this lot is comprised of mixed heirloom varieties without specific selection of varieties that comes with several smallholder farmers producing cherries at a time. The cherries are sent to the Suke Washing station where they're processed in the traditional washed fashion - floated, depulped, washed, and

items.title: Chiroso Washed Las Perlitas
items.desc:
A washed Chiroso from Las Perlitas in Antioquia, Colombia, sourced through Coffee Quest. Smallholder deliveries are cupped separately and combined when their profiles complement one another.
Bright, juicy and sweet, with orange, prune and almond in the cup. We roast it to work beautifully as both filter and espresso.

items.title: Cherry Ripe Blend
items.desc:
This coffee is born out of a simple question - how can we make an espresso blend that's the most fruity as possible, while still being clear and clean. We have been working on this lot for several months, starting right from sourcing. We worked hand in hand with our friends at Cofinet to source these components and design this blend around 3 particular lots.
Firstly a Washed and Natural Caturra - these set the base for our blend providing a fruity, yet well structured base. The last component is a small amount of a Cherry co-fermented coffee from Jairo Arcilla. This is what gives us that big b

items.title: Rose Rejects
items.desc:
Rose Rejects is coffee that didn’t make it into our main lineup.
It’s a mix of beans rejected by our colour sorter — including quakers and beans that are visually over-roasted — alongside roasted batches that missed our internal targets by being too light, too dark, or otherwise outside spec. Nothing unsafe, nothing adulterated, just coffee that didn’t meet the standard we set for Rose.
This is not a curated blend and it’s not meant to be expressive or particularly tasty. Expect a very basic cup. Sometimes flat, sometimes rough, sometimes fine — but never special. If you’re looking for clarity

items.title: The House Blend
items.desc:
This is a special "House Blend" that we've designed specifically for use on Espresso machines / Bialetti. It's an easy drinking coffee that has a well developed roast profile to make it easy to extract, while still keeping recognisable flavours of the origins. We would call this a "Medium - Dark" roast. Not so much that the beans are all oily, but developed enough to have Low Acidity, Smooth Body, and mostly chocolatey flavour notes.
All the coffees we use in this are Specialty coffee, but with very approachable taste profiles and qualities. We've sourced these lots either direct from farmers,

items.title: The Bedtime Blend
items.desc:
This is a blend that we've designed especially to be as delicious as non-decaffeinated coffee - to be used for Espresso/Bialetti brewing and goes amazing as both a black coffee, and with milk.
We believe that decaffeinated coffee doesn't have to come at the sacrifice of quality - so we created this Decaf blend that is as delicious as full strength coffee. Generally you will find more sweetness and acidity, as the balance with the bitter caffeine has been removed. In some of these coffees we find more spice, and malt notes from the decaf process, and some darker roasted notes from the darker ro

items.title: Jingle Beans Holiday Blend
items.desc: Behold! A coffee is born. 'Tis the freaking season and what have you! Oh, Jingle Beans, oh Jingle Beans, our annual ho-li-day blend. Each year we go out of our way to make this blend as seasonally outlandish as we can. This year, two coffees from Ethiopia — a washed and a naturally processed — triumphantly coalesce into the best interpretation of drinkable fruit cake in a cup. Jingle Beans, Jingle Beans, Jingle all the beans.

items.title: David Muñoz - Honduras
items.desc: For the second consecutive year, we kick off Honduran season with a coffee from David Muñoz, a producer who’s been a mainstay on the Tandem menu for a decade. David grows multiple varieties on his roughly 3 hectare farm, Nueva Esperanza, in Santa Barbara, but the majority is Pacas. This 100% Pacas lot is soft and sweetness-driven. We taste a familiar, balanced cup with flavors of caramel, milk chocolate, toasted nuts, and gentle plum-like acidity.

items.title: Arley Arboleda - Colombia
items.desc: This small lot from Arley Arboleda is another excellent Chiroso from Urrao. Arley is a 36-year-old, second-generation producer growing Chiroso at 2,100 masl across two hectares. He learned coffee farming from his father as a teenager and purchased the land for Finca Los Guaicos in 2022 with the specific goal of cultivating exclusively Chiroso. As with many producers in the region, Arley uses the cochadas method, a regional processing practice in which each day’s harvest is depulped and added to the same fermentation tank throughout the week. Once the tank is full, the coffee is washed together

items.title: Chelbesa - Ethiopia
items.desc: We’re excited to have back on our menu for another season this bright, refreshing classic from the Chelbesa One Washing Station. Approximately 1,000 smallholder farmers deliver cherry to Chelbesa One, one of seven washing stations across Ethiopia managed by SNAP Coffee. Cherries are sorted, floated, and depulped, then dry fermented in tanks for 48-72 hours before being washed and placed to dry on raised beds for 7-10 days. Coffees from this station are typically pristine and elegant. Expect a crisp, lightly effervescent profile with white tea aromatics and flavors of grapefruit, melon, and pea

items.title: Kibingo - Kenya
items.desc: This washed field blend from Kibingo Estate is another stellar coffee sourced via Kamavindi Coffee Labs. Established in 1957 with just 100 trees — the maximum allotment for Kenyan growers under colonial law at the time — Kibingo has since grown into one of the country’s most highly regarded estate farms. The estate won Kenya’s Taste of Harvest competition in 2024, and owner Anthony Kimani has continued investing in farm-level and processing infrastructure, with plans to expand beyond its current 6,000 trees. In the cup, we taste ripe red fruits like pomegranate and raspberry, sweet spice, and

items.title: Oneska - Kenya
items.desc: Oneska is the small estate farm of Onesmus Njagi, a retired schoolteacher, and his wife, Karen, on the slopes of Mount Kenya in Embu County. Last fall, we visited ahead of harvest and toured their four hectares, where they grow the traditional SL-28 and SL-34 varieties at good altitude and under ideal growing conditions. items.desc: This year, we purchased a split share of Alma Pineda’s washed Gesha lot, one of our top-scoring coffees from the 2026 Honduras Cup of Excellence (CoE). Alma’s coffees have placed at the Honduras CoE before, including third in 2019 and second in 2024, with this lot placing eighth in the Exotic Varieties category. Her farm, El Limo, sits at 1650 masl in Santa Barbara, where nearly all the Honduran coffee on our menu is grown. items.desc: This is the first of three Pink Bourbon lots we’ll be featuring from the main harvest at Finca Costa Rica, Faver Ninco’s 10-hectare farm in Santa Maria. At just over 2,000 masl, Finca Costa Rica experiences cooler temperatures than much of the region, with more limited sunlight and less regular rainfall. items.title: Sun Lamp Decaf
items.desc:
“I might as well be drinking tea*,” you say to no one in particular as you drink another cup of lousy decaffeinated coffee. Don’t feel defeated by bad decaf. Turn to Tandem’s brighter, sweeter Sun Lamp. With hints of marshmallow, graham cracker and green grape, let the surprising flavors of Sun Lamp reimagine what decaffeinated coffee can be and leave the anxiety behind.
*No offense to tea. We love tea.

items.title: West End Blues
items.desc: Traditional in name only, West End Blues is a complex blend of flavors and textures. Fruity but not fruit-forward, grounded in chocolate and sparkling with zesty notes of baking spices and tea, WEB shines when combined with milk but stands on its own as a killer drip coffee.

items.title: Stoker
items.desc: Sometimes you want a delicious, no-nonsense cup of coffee, beloved by metalheads and hardcore grandmothers alike. That’s why Tandem shed its “Light Roaster” mantle to create our version of a “Kinda Dark” roasted coffee. Inspired by late-night diner runs, hot donuts, and arctic blasts, Stoker’s pleasantly sweet roastiness will carry you through the day.

items.title: Time & Temperature
items.desc: Effervescent, electric, and just plain cool, Time and Temperature is Tandem’s signature espresso blend. Perfect for dancing alone or with friends, it doubles as a delightful drip coffee. However you enjoy its crisp acidity and punchy sweetness, it’s our embodiment of “Spreading Joy” in every cup.

items.desc:
History
Los Pirineos Gesha Natural comes from fifth-generation producer Diego Baraona, continuing a family coffee-growing legacy of more than 130 years in Usulután, El Salvador. Grown at 1,400 masl on the slopes of a standalone volcano, the coffee benefits from fertile volcanic soils and a distinctive microclimate of sunny days and cool ocean breezes. Diego is dedicated to preserving and developing the farm’s diversity, cultivating around 20 coffee varieties and maintaining a nursery with approximately 70 varieties. items.desc:
History
Israel Jamioy is a second-generation coffee producer from the Inga Indigenous community of Aponte, Nariño, Colombia, where coffee has become a symbol of resilience, cultural identity and a brighter future. Working within the collectively governed Resguardo Inga de Aponte, Israel is part of a community that has transformed its agricultural landscape, replacing illegal crops with coffee cultivation. Despite significant challenges, including a devastating landslide in 2024, the community remains deeply committed to its land and coffee-growing traditions.

items.title: La Indonesia Colombia Washed
items.desc:
History
From Finca La Indonesia in Nariño, Colombia, this coffee is produced by Frank Rivas Torres and his siblings, continuing a family tradition spanning over 80 years. Now in our fifth year of purchasing their coffee, we’re proud to continue this relationship built on quality and craftsmanship. Carefully washed through an extended fermentation process and slowly dried on raised beds, it reflects Frank’s precise, quality-focused approach. Grown alongside diverse fruit and shade trees, this coffee celebrates family heritage, innovation, and the rich coffee culture of Nariño.

items.desc:
History
From Nuwa Senchi in Amazonas, Peru, this coffee is the first harvest from Sonia Diaz’s Geisha, Marshell, and Bourbon plants. It is also our first purchase from Sonia, following our visit to her farm and continued collaboration in Jaén. Grown at 1,800–1,950 meters above sea level, this coffee reflects Sonia’s focus on quality, traceability, and careful processing. Through Nuwa Senchi, she is also creating new opportunities for Amazonian women and the next generation of coffee producers.

items.title: Kigari AA
items.desc:
History
Our relationship with Kigari spans three years, with coffee purchased in 2022, 2023 and 2026. Based in the highlands of Meru County, Kenya, Kigari brings together farmers across four wet mills, producing exceptional coffee at 1,600–1,900 masl. The cooperative is deeply committed to its farmers, providing access to pre-financing, farm inputs on credit, school-fee support and emergency funds, practical support that helps farming families invest in their futures and sustain coffee production year after year.

History
This is our first year working with Emerson Felipe Narváez at El Turpial and the third coffee to be released after Sudan Rume and Laurina. Emerson is a Q Grader and highly driven producer who experiments with rare varieties and advanced processing techniques. This lot is an Ethiopian Landrace, rarely grown in Colombia, and has been carefully adapted to the farm’s high-altitude conditions and microclimate.

items.desc:
History
This washed Caturra is produced by smallholder families of the Indigenous Inga community of Aponte, Nariño, at approximately 2,150 meters above sea level.
The high-altitude environment, cool temperatures, and mineral-rich volcanic soils support slow cherry maturation, healthy cultivation, and exceptionally sweet, complex coffees. Expect notes of brown sugar, yellow plum and apple.

This is our second time purchasing coffee from Danche Washing Station, after our first lot in 2022 (Sami Danche Øko). items.title: Apax Lab - Jamm
items.desc:
JAMM is formulated to bring roundness and will accentuate the lingering sweetness and creamy mouthfeel of your brew. With just a few drops, it enhances body and softens sharp edges, delivering a smooth and full-flavoured cup.
Used by World Coffee Champions and trusted by leading cafés worldwide , JAMM is the go-to profile for coffee enthusiasts looking to balance complex or funky coffees with ease.
Enhances body and mouthfeel
Increases sweetness and balance
Smooths sharp or funky notes
Perfect for naturals, experimental fermentations, and winey coffees

items.title: Apax Lab - Lylac
items.desc:
LYLAC is designed to extend the finish and highlight delicate aromatics in your coffee. It refines texture, reduces dryness, and reveals a silky, elegant cup with a long, clean aftertaste.
Favoured by coffee competitors and leading cafés worldwide , LYLAC is the secret weapon for showcasing refined coffees and elegant filter brews.
Highlights floral aromatics
Creates a silky, elegant mouthfeel
Extends and cleans the finish
Reduces dryness in lighter profiles

items.title: Apax Lab - Tonik
items.desc:
TONIK is formulated to enhance the vibrant acidity and bring a crisp, juicy kick to your brews. With just a few drops, you can unlock brightness and clarity that make washed coffees and lively fruit-forward profiles shine.
Trusted by over 200 National Champions and 90% of competitors at the 2025 World Brewers Cup , TONIK is a proven tool for baristas, cafés, and home brewers worldwide.
Elevates acidity, vibrancy, and clarity
Adds a lively, juicy character to your coffee
Easy to use in cafés, competitions, or at home
Perfect for washed coffees and fruit-driven profiles

In the highlands of western Guatemala, smallholder producers in Huehuetenango farm steep, fertile slopes where coffee sustains much of the local economy. Working collectively through the Regional Select programme, they’ve built a system that rewards quality while keeping value close to origin. This lot was crafted to capture the essence of Huehuetenango's flavour.

That said, we remain open-minded and keen to find high-quality lots from all origins. Aceh Gayo is a great example of that. Through natural processing, its producers have retained the generous body and bold fruit we associate with Indonesian coffee, while creating a cup of remarkable complexity and winey depth.

The factory is one of several owned and operated by the Mutheka Farmers’ Cooperative Society, who bring together the work of local smallholders. These farmers typically grow coffee alongside crops like maize, bananas and beans, and on average tend to around 250 coffee trees each.

Gera Seriti is grown on the high plateaus of Gera, within Ethiopia’s Limmu region. This coffee comes from a 2.5 hectare plot managed by producer Mustafa Mohamed Ali, whose family has been cultivating coffee in this region since the mid-20th century. Today, he carefully maintains his inherited farms with organic practices, reinforcing the diversity of the landscape, and also produces honey and milk.

items.desc:
High in the mountains of Nariño, Colombia, the Inga community of Aponte are descendants of the pre-Hispanic Incas. Historically, the community has been fairly isolated, however during the 1990s the region became a target for guerrilla groups and traffickers, who forced farmers to produce poppy and heroin. The tribe has worked hard to reclaim its land and livelihoods, and coffee cultivation has played a significant part in that change. Today, smallholders farm at an average of 2150 masl, in soils enriched by the nearby Galeras volcano.

José cultivates Caturra, Colombia, and Castillo varieties, alongside oranges, lemons, and avocados. Coffee farming runs in the family; his grandfather was a pioneer of coffee production in Pozo Negro, helping to establish the practice in the community. Today, Andrés continues this legacy, working alongside his wife Teresa and their family across the farm. They grow the IH-90 varietal, a hybrid developed in Honduras in the 80s and 90s.

items.title: Kaffebønner Oslo Mørkbrent
items.desc:
Oslo Mørkbrent er en kaffeblanding laget for dem som liker en kraftig og fyldig kopp kaffe eller espresso. Vårt team har selektert ulike kaffepartier og brent blandingen for å fremheve sødme og få en rik munnfølelse.
Innholdet i blandingen vil variere etter sesong, men smaken vil alltid være mot nougat, tørket frukt og kakao.
Oslo Mørkbrent passer både til espresso og kaffemaskiner, samt for de av oss som liker litt krutt i trakteren.
Innholder 2 x 250g Oslo Mørkbrent

items.title: Kaffebønner Østmarka
items.desc:
Østmarka er vår sesongbaserte espressoblanding. Espressoblandingen består av spesielt utvalgte kaffepartier valgt for sine attributter for å få en ren, søt og balansert espresso.
Innholdet i blandingen vil variere etter sesong, men vårt mål er at dette skal være en fruktig espresso-blanding med god balanse og fin sødme. Du vil ofte finne kaffe fra både Amerika og Afrika i denne blandingen, men partiene vil variere fra sesong til sesong.
Innholder 2 x 250g Østmarka espresso

items.title: XMAS COFFEE FINCA MAJAHUAL - ESPRESSO/ DARKER
items.desc:
The perfect finishing touch to your Christmas table, or a gift for a friend: a full-bodied Christmas coffee from Finca Majahual in El Salvador. 🎄
This natural-processed Red Bourbon from the Finca Majahual farm is our richer Christmas coffee option, and a perfect companion to the Christmas dessert table.
The coffee has the juicy, full body typical of natural processing. In the cup you can taste the soft sweetness and fruitiness of Christmas, with notes of dark cherry and brown sugar. It works especially well as espresso or filter coffee for anyone who enjoys a slightly fuller-bodied, medium-dar

items.title: XMAS COFFEE LA CORDILLERA - FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
A fruity treat for Christmas morning or a gift for a friend: La Cordillera Christmas coffee from Nicaragua 🎄
This year’s lighter Christmas coffee comes from northern Nicaragua. In this bright, washed coffee you can taste the sweetness of pear, marzipan and the roundness of milk chocolate. It’s the kind of coffee you’ll want to brew by the potful for the Christmas table and serve with gingerbread cookies or Christmas pastries.
For those who prefer a fuller-bodied coffee, we also recommend our Finca Majahual Christmas coffee or the Christmas Coffee Duo featuring two coffees.

items.title: SURPLUS COFFEES
items.desc:
What makes it a surplus coffee?
We want to make sure that every bag of coffee we’ve roasted and packed with love gets enjoyed, so from time to time we put bags left over from mix-ups or surplus on sale at a small discount.
Test roast: Our coffee selection changes often, so we roast test batches regularly while we look for the best possible roast profile for each coffee. These are excellent test roasts of new coffees whose profiles we may still fine-tune, or for which we haven’t yet finalised detailed tasting notes and other details.
Surplus coffee: Sometimes a week’s roast leaves us with more

items.title: CASA VIEJA, GUATEMALA - FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
This coffee from Ismael Quinteros Orantes’s small Casa Vieja farm in Santa Rosa, Guatemala, offers notes of nectarine, marmalade and milk chocolate.
On the slopes of El Volcancito, at 1,760 metres above sea level, Ismael grows coffee on just over two hectares. He is the third generation of coffee farmers in his family. Around 60 years ago, his grandfather grew both sugarcane and coffee and found that coffee was the more profitable crop. items.title: DON ELI, COSTA RICA - FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
This washed Don Eli from the mountains of Tarrazú offers notes of s weet grape, mandarin and fudge-like sweetness. The mouthfeel is juicy and smooth.
The coffee comes from the Montero family, who helped build Tarrazú’s specialty coffee scene and guide the region’s shift from traditional coffee farming toward quality-focused micro mills and direct trade. Carlos Montero founded the Don Eli micro mill in 2014 and named it after his father, Eli. Today, processing is led by Carlos’s son, Jacob Montero, who keeps refining his methods so that the character of each harvest can shine through.

items.title: EL RENACER NATURAL, COSTA RICA - FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
This is the third coffee of the season from the Ureña family’s Café Rivense farm. This time it’s a naturally processed Casiopea. Its full, smooth body is complemented by notes of blueberry, plum wine and pecan.
Unlike the farm’s two previous coffees ( La Catarata Honey and La Catarata Anaerobic Natural ), this one comes from a plot called El Renacer. The plot sits at 1,700 metres and is planted with Casiopea. This relatively rare variety is an Arabica F1 hybrid, a cross between Caturra and a wild Ethiopian strain. items.title: TIMANCO, COLOMBIA - ESPRESSO / DARKER
items.desc:
Here’s that crowd-pleasing, reliable everyday espresso. This washed Colombian coffee also works beautifully as a darker-roasted filter coffee. Expect notes of ripe, full-bodied plum and red apple, with a brown sugar sweetness in the finish.
Timaná is one of Colombia’s oldest indigenous settlements. The region is known for its unique geography and waterways: it’s surrounded not only by the Andes but also by the Magdalena and Golden rivers. This combination of geographical factors gives the area’s coffees their balanced, layered character.

items.title: LA GUACA, BOURBON AJI, COLOMBIA - FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
This coffee, made from the (still) rare Bourbon Ají variety, comes from José Herman Salazar and his family farm, Finca La Guaca, in the Pitalito area of southern Huila, Colombia. It is a carefully grown and precisely processed coffee from a family business with a long-term focus on improving quality. The cup is clean and nuanced, with notes of apple pie and star fruit and the sweetness of panela.

items.title: LA CATARATA ANAEROBIC NATURAL, COSTA RICA
items.desc:
An anaerobically fermented, natural processed Red Catuai coffee from the Ureña family, at Café Rivense's La Catarata farm in Costa Rica. A full-bodied and sweet coffee, with the anaerobic fermentation adding a distinctly layered character to the cup. Expect notes of fruit jam, cacao nibs and caramel, with a velvety mouthfeel and restrained acidity. This coffee pairs exceptionally well with milk.
The Ureña family is no stranger to GLC. We've been buying coffee from them for several years now, and in December 2025, Lauri and Aleksi had the chance to visit their Café Rivense del Chirripó farm in

items.title: BOMBE ANAEROBIC NATURAL, ETHIOPIA - FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
Coffees like this don't show up in the GLC lineup all the time, but right now, one does. A special lot, anaerobically fermented and naturally processed from Ethiopia. Light fermentation combined with the balance and sweetness that natural processing brings makes this one a real treat. Expect notes of papaya, bergamot and dark chocolate.

items.title: LA CATARATA HONEY, COSTA RICA - FILTER COFFEE
items.desc:
We're delighted to bring this Costa Rican coffee back into our lineup again this year. This coffee from the Ureña family's Café Rivense farm bursts with sweet juiciness! In the flavor you'll find the fruitiness like plum and juiciness of ripe black cherry along with the after taste of cocoa nibs, with a mild acidity that's well balanced with the mouthfeel.
This coffee comes from Café Rivense del Chirripó, a family-owned smallholder farm founded in 2005 by Régulo Ureña and Isabel Rojas in southern Costa Rica. The farm's quality work has been recognized in competitions such as the Cup of Excelle

items.desc: Invented in the early 1930s, the Moka pot (also known as the Italian coffee maker) revolutionized the way we prepare coffee at home. In 2019, architect David Chipperfield redesigned this iconic coffee maker, which we love thanks to the details of its cast aluminum model.

items.desc: A special meeting of two coffees from Guatemala and Costa Rica, capturing all the magic of the holidays. The spicy notes of gingerbread, the bright acidity of cranberry, and the delicate sweetness of vanilla create a warm, harmonious blend, perfect for enjoying the most special moments of Christmas. To give as a gift, share, or simply savor.

items.title: Ethiopia • Tome • Natural
items.desc:
From the highlands of the Guji region in Ethiopia, at an altitude of 1,900 to 2,200 meters, comes a coffee that expresses the full elegance and aromatic complexity of this extraordinary region. Grown on the Oboleyan farm, this Heirloom variety Single Origin coffee is processed using the Natural process, which brings out its sweetness and delicate aromatic notes.
In the cup, the elegant floral notes of jasmine are intertwined with the lively freshness of lemongrass , leaving room for the soft, enveloping sweetness of honey. The result is a harmonious, refined coffee with balanced acidity, a ple

items.title: Ethiopia Worka Wuri
items.desc:
In the heart of Gedeb, one of the most renowned areas of the Yirgacheffe region, this single-origin coffee is grown at an altitude of 1,900 to 2,100 meters. Here, the cool climate, wide temperature swings, and fertile soils allow the cherries to ripen slowly, developing extraordinary aromatic complexity.
The Heirloom varieties, ancient indigenous Ethiopian cultivars, give this coffee an elegant, nuanced profile that expresses the full character of its terroir. The washed process enhances its clarity and brightness, highlighting the transparency of its aromatic notes and the pleasant liveliness

items.title: Ethiopia Aricha Wubanchi
items.desc:
A single-origin coffee from Aricha Wubanchi, in the heart of the Yirgacheffe region, grown at an altitude of 2,200 meters.
Made from Heirloom varieties and processed using the washed method, this coffee showcases the finesse of Ethiopia’s high altitudes. A bright, clean cup where lively acidity intertwines with delicate sweetness.
Notes of peach, lime, and berries come through on the palate, with an elegant, fresh, and lingering aromatic profile.

items.title: Honduras Finca El Puente • Anaerobic Natural
items.desc:
We’re talking about the same botanical variety, Catuai, and the same processing method. The only difference is the fermentation method: this time, it’s 100% anaerobic fermentation, meaning entirely without oxygen.
This coffee offers a rounder, more complex acidity, with fruity notes reminiscent of pineapple. Its sweetness is intense and recalls dried fruit, like raisins, with a rich body and a lingering, sweet, syrupy aftertaste, enriched with hints of honey.

items.title: Honduras Finca El Puente • Marsellesa • washed
items.desc:
Finca El Puente Marsellesa Washed comes from Marcala, Honduras, at an altitude of 1,550 meters. The Marsellesa variety is processed using the Washed method, which helps enhance its clarity and aromatic definition.
In the cup, it has a sweet, fresh, and fruity profile: citrus notes of orange meet the sweetness of red apple and cane sugar, creating a pleasant, harmonious balance.
A coffee with a lively, well-defined character, where freshness and sweetness come together in a clean, balanced, enjoyable cup.

items.title: Honduras Finca El Puente • Anacafe • washed
items.desc:
From Honduras, in the Marcala region, comes a coffee grown at Finca El Puente, at an altitude of 1,550 meters. The Anacafe variety, processed using the Washed method, produces a clean, sweet cup where hints of honey meet the smoothness of maple syrup and the rich notes of caramel.
A profile built around sweetness, with full, harmonious flavors unfolding in the cup and leading to a pleasantly lingering finish.

items.title: Honduras Finca El Puente • Geisha • Washed
items.desc:
Finca El Puente "Geisha Washed" is a single-origin coffee grown using the prized Geisha variety and processed using the washed method. This precise and meticulous process brings out the coffee's clarity and aromatic definition.
Its sensory notes reveal a floral, fresh, and fruity profile. The delicate mango meets the vibrant freshness of lime and the juicy sweetness of pineapple, creating an elegant, balanced cup full of nuance.
Considered one of the most exclusive coffees in our selection, it stands out for its aromatic complexity and elegance in the cup. A Geisha that reveals, sip after sip,

items.title: Uganda • Bantu Blossom
items.desc:
From Uganda comes a coffee that tells the story of a region still waiting to be explored. Grown at an altitude of 1,600 to 1,800 meters by Agri Evolve, it brings together the SL14 and SL28 varieties, both deeply rooted in the history of coffee cultivation in this part of Africa.
The natural process brings out its sweeter, fruitier character, creating a rich cup full of nuances. Blueberry stands out with its juicy note, followed by the mellow sweetness of chestnut and a deeper finish of dark chocolate.
A profile that balances fruit, sweetness, and intensity, revealing a side of Uganda worth dis

items.title: Colombia • Los Nogales • Bourbon
items.desc:
Grown at an altitude of 1,750 meters at Finca Nogales, this harvest showcases the exceptional qualities of the Bourbon Pimienta variety, processed using the meticulous “Dark Room Dried” natural method, designed to preserve its full aromatic complexity.
At the first sip, rich, creamy notes of apricot yogurt emerge, blending gently with hints of banana before giving way to a delicate violet finish. A vibrant, enveloping, unforgettable cup that turns every sip into a moment to savor.

items.title: Panama Finca Lerida • pacamara
items.desc: From the highlands of Alto Quiel, Panama , at 1,700 meters, comes the Pacamara from Finca Lérida . Processed using the natural method, it offers a rich, fruity profile in the cup, where the sweetness of honey meets the juicy notes of plum and the aromatic brightness of orange peel . A coffee with a bold character that tells the full story of its origin.

items.title: Panama Finca Lerida • natural
items.desc: In the highlands of Alto Quiel, Panama , at 1,700 meters, Finca Lerida is home to a Geisha that tells the story of its land with every sip. Processed using the natural method, it reveals an intense, nuanced aromatic profile: the floral fragrance of jasmine opens the tasting, making way for the tropical sweetness of mango and the juicy brightness of blueberry . A medley of aromas that makes this cup complex and surprising, and a highlight of Best of Panama 2026.

items.title: Panama Finca Lerida • washed
items.desc: Fresh and floral, this Geisha Washed from Finca Lerida expresses all the finesse of Panama’s high altitudes. Lemongrass opens the sip with a lively note, followed by the delicate aromas of elderflower and the subtle sweetness of honeydew melon . A clean, fragrant cup with remarkable aromatic clarity.

items.title: Panama Finca Lerida • honey

A coffee crafted for those seeking balance and aromatic clarity, ideal both as a pour-over and as an espresso.

items.desc:

Uganda to reprezentantka ciemniejszego, bardziej charakternego wypału. To taki cięższy singiel z korzennym klimatem. Gorzka czekolada daje bazę i lekką goryczkę, orzech włoski wnosi suchszy, bardziej wytrawny akcent, a cynamon otwiera przyprawowy kierunek. W espresso wyczujecie ciemne owoce i kwasowość w tle. Malina jest tutaj reprezentantką wszystkich owoców suszonych – idących w słodycz, nie w kwasowość. Migdał daje spokojną, słodkawą orzechowość, a mleczna czekolada wygładza całość. Z mlekiem poczujecie karmelkowo-śmietankowy trop niczym z Werther’s Original.
